standard_prerequisites.name: Finite planar range hypergraphs and general position
standard_prerequisites.statement: An axis-parallel strip captures exactly the input points between two vertical or two horizontal lines. The finitely many freely placed points can have distinct x- and y-coordinates while satisfying the author strict inequalities.
standard_prerequisites.use: Choose strip boundaries between coordinates, and enlarge a captured set of at most m points to exactly m points by moving a boundary when needed.

standard_prerequisites.use: Track the exact cluster sizes and the consequences of every captured m-edge having one or two selected vertices.

Assuming X missed, force D missed by a last-hit suffix/prefix switch and propagate the E,F,G,H,I,J,K constraints to three hits in one strip.
Force all original clusters hit, obtain three hits beside a selected anchor, and extend captured strips to size m using distinct coordinates.

proof_roadmap.step: Set the parameters and separated global rows/columns. If all local2a-clusters are hit, the two sides of a selected anchor yield the contradiction.
Specify the ten-cluster local geometry, original cardinality diagram, and opposite diagonal orders for B,C.

Three m-edge obligations and a one-hit budget force E empty and G,H hit; then I empty, J,K hit, contradicting the shallow bound on a completion of G union J union K.

difficulty_reason: The two-axis gadget and exact-cardinality switch are substantive combinatorial construction obligations; not a direct consequence of the bottomless-rectangle counterexample. Source542 convex-hull cardinality is an explicitly disclosed notation slip, interpreted by535 and author figure.

compared.difference: The old claim concerns infinite arithmetic-progression difference sets and polychromatic coloring, not finite strip hitting sets.

The other prepared claim forbids3-shallow hitting for bottomless rectangles via an A/B/C gadget and a triple-window case split. This claim forbids2-shallow hitting for single axis-parallel strips and requires the different ten-auxiliary-cluster forcing mechanism.

editorial_notes: The original two PNG figures are included with their basenames. Their black lines are visible on the white PDF page; the transparent images were also checked in the official PDF page13 for the local cluster sizes.

Source542 puts conv around projected point sets inside a cardinality equal to a. The construction may choose distinct x- and y-coordinates within every cluster. This preserves all strict cluster-order inequalities and lets a strip with fewer than m captured points be enlarged to exactly m, one point at a time. This is the extension step already invoked at592 and needed at545.

The source figures give |X|=2a, |B|=|C|=m-2a, |D|=2a-1, |E|=|F|=m-2a-b+1=a-b/2, |G|=|H|=b, |I|=m-2b, and |J|=|K|=2b. These are transcribed here for legibility; the original figures and prose remain the author proof.

The auxiliary clusters for distinct local gadgets occupy separate horizontal bands outside all global J_i strips, and the complete local gadget stays inside its own reserved vertical I interval, as required by source539/547.

review_checkpoints: The set {b_k} union B-prime union C-prime has m-2a+1 points, so after adjoining D of size2a-1 it is an exact m-edge; two known hits therefore force D empty.
D+E+G, D+E+H and D+F+H are exact m-edges captured vertically. E+F+H+B is an exact m-edge captured horizontally, imposing the one-hit bound on E+F+H.
If E had a hit, the one-hit bound would empty both F and H, contradicting the F+H obligation. Thus G and H each have a hit. I+G+H is an m-edge, so I is empty. I+J and I+K are m-edges, so J,K are hit.
G+J+K is captured vertically and has5b points; m>=5b permits enlargement without losing its three hits.
The global half-row includes a points from X_i,1,2a from one of X_i,2/X_i,3 and the anchor, hence3a+1<=m; its known hits persist under enlargement.
